verifier_reason: test_outputs.py::test_tasks_cancel_below_max_concurrent: The test failed in the call phase due to an assertion error

items.name: Readability
items.evidence: Single-letter and cryptic names in business logic (`t = next(task_iter)`, `wt`, `e`, `coro`). There are no docstrings, and the non-obvious SIGINT, shield-loop and `uncancel` logic has no comments.

items.name: Maintainability
items.evidence: `run_tasks` runs about 110 lines (diff lines 10-119), with the nested `on_sigint` and `worker` closures sharing nonlocal mutable state (`stop`, `interrupted`, `interrupt_count`). Signal handling, worker pool and error aggregation are all in one function.

items.name: Robustness
items.evidence: Uses a custom `signal.signal(SIGINT, on_sigint)` hack, the kind of signal handling the project conventions rule out. `while not clean_fut.done(): try: await asyncio.shield(...) except CancelledError: pass` swallows cancellations, alongside forced `uncancel()` loops. All three hidden cancel tests fail.

items.name: Failures and degenerate arguments
items.evidence: Returns early on an empty list and raises `ValueError` when `max_concurrent <= 0`. A failing task sets `stop`, cancels the other workers and its error is re-raised (`raise exceptions[0]`). The finally block gathers all workers, so cleanup runs and queued tasks never start.

items.name: Required signature and import behaviour
items.name_zh: 签名与导入行为符合要求
items.evidence: The async signature and annotations match, callables are invoked lazily as worker slots free up, and import has no side effects (stdlib only). It deviates a little: `coro = t() if callable(t) else t` plus `inspect.isawaitable` accepts non-callables and silently skips results that aren't awaitable, and each call swaps the process SIGINT handler.
